name: These Arms Are Snakes
label: Jade Tree
lede: A Seattle band built from the wreckage of Botch and Kill Sadie, named because the name sounded ridiculous, that survived a semi-truck, a Christian metalcore tour and four drummers before its gear gave out at the last show.

eras.title: Out of the Botch wreckage
eras.text: In February 2002 Botch fell apart, and bassist Brian Cook went looking for something stranger. With singer Steve Snere from Kill Sadie, guitarist Ryan Frederiksen from Nineironspitfire, drummer Joe Preston and keyboardist Jesse Robertson, he built a Seattle band that treated post-hardcore like a haunted carnival.

years.h: [[Botch|72448406-ba82-43a7-9e13-d9a47ff333f4]] breaks up, freeing bassist Brian Cook
years.p: Botch splits after tension between drummer Tim Latona and guitarist Dave Knudson, and plays its last show on June 15, 2002 at the Showbox in Seattle. Brian Cook is already on to his next band.

years.cap: These Arms Are Snakes · via Discogs
years.h: These Arms Are Snakes forms in Seattle
years.p: Steve Snere, Ryan Frederiksen, Brian Cook, Joe Preston and Jesse Robertson start the band; Bill Quinby plays guitar for 2002 only. They pick the name These Arms Are Snakes because it sounded ridiculous and like no other band name.
years.xp: The members came from three Seattle bands: Brian Cook from [[Botch|72448406-ba82-43a7-9e13-d9a47ff333f4]], Steve Snere from [[Kill Sadie|1b2717df-9eea-423b-8ee6-6d678d0cd35a]] and Ryan Frederiksen from Nineironspitfire. Before the debut EP they cut a four-song demo that stayed unreleased for twenty years.

years.h: This Is Meant to Hurt You, the debut EP on Jade Tree
years.p: These Arms Are Snakes' first release, and the only one with Jesse Robertson as full-time keyboardist. AllMusic gave it three stars and called the lyrics smart and cunning.

eras.title: A semi-truck and the Totally Badical Tour
eras.text: The band lost its keyboardist and then its drummer, and the drummer's goodbye nearly took everyone with it. Stripped to four, These Arms Are Snakes made Oxeneers and then spent a winter as the odd band out on a tour of Christian metalcore.

years.h: Keyboardist Jesse Robertson quits over touring
years.p: Jesse Robertson leaves after disagreeing with the band about how it toured. As a four-piece, These Arms Are Snakes goes for sparer arrangements and more room to run around the stage.

years.cap: These Arms Are Snakes · via Discogs
years.h: Joe Preston's farewell ends in a crash with a semi
years.p: After drummer Joe Preston's farewell show, Preston and the rest of These Arms Are Snakes are in a van that collides with a semi-truck. Erin Tate, of [[Kill Sadie|1b2717df-9eea-423b-8ee6-6d678d0cd35a]] and [[Minus the Bear|c1e98e4a-4628-4c89-a7a6-0e0171600b05]], takes over the drums.
years.xp: Wikipedia records the crash but not where it happened or who was hurt. Erin Tate drums on the debut album Oxeneers and stays until 2005.

years.h: Like a Virgin: a split with Harkonen
years.p: These Arms Are Snakes and Harkonen share a split on Hydra Head and Mind Over Matter, with a joint track called Touched for the Very First Time.

years.h: Oxeneers, the debut album, on Jade Tree
years.p: Co-produced with [[Matt Bayles|e294077f-71eb-401f-a36a-f2dbcbd75863]] at Litho and Spectre South, with Erin Tate on drums. Jade Tree issues the CD and Second Nature the vinyl; Pitchfork gives it 7.6.
years.xp: The last track, Idaho, hides an untitled piece that starts at 6:36. Bayles also plays extra guitar and percussion, and [[Ben Verellen|15d611a9-28df-4042-a35d-12c6410cdd5b]] and Botch's Dave Knudson are among the guests.

years.h: The odd band out on [[Underoath|674a7e8c-9682-419a-8e05-2358e28b5359]]'s Totally Badical Tour
years.p: Opening for Underoath with The Chariot, Hopesfall and Fear Before the March of Flames, These Arms Are Snakes gets a cool reception. The band clashes with Underoath over religion and politics.
years.xp: The band said selling merch on the tour felt like an empty gesture. The arguments over faith didn't end when the tour did: they fed loosely into the themes of the next album, Easter.

years.h: Two drummers in one year; Chris Common stays
years.p: Erin Tate leaves, [[Ben Verellen|15d611a9-28df-4042-a35d-12c6410cdd5b]] joins and quits without explanation, and [[Chris Common|680f3d25-dc62-4f1d-a5e4-6c56f785287d]] takes the drum stool. Common will also produce the band's next two albums.

eras.title: An album called Easter
eras.text: With Chris Common on drums and behind the desk, These Arms Are Snakes made its heaviest-thinking record, circling religion after a tour spent arguing about it. Then they toured constantly, from Thrice to Mastodon.

years.h: Good Friday 7-inch and a first Suicide Squeeze release
years.p: These Arms Are Snakes puts out the Good Friday 7-inch on Suicide Squeeze, and gives the song Old Paradise to the label's Slaying Since 1996 compilation.

years.h: Easter, the second album · Jade Tree JT1118
years.p: Produced by Chris Common and the band, with [[Matt Bayles|e294077f-71eb-401f-a36a-f2dbcbd75863]] engineering. Religion runs through it, most plainly in Perpetual Bris, though Steve Snere said it wasn't meant as direct religious commentary.
years.xp: Snere said he was writing about the bigger picture of life and existence. The friction with Underoath on the Totally Badical Tour loosely shaped the record's direction. Brian Cook and Demian Johnston made the artwork.

years.h: On the road for Easter with Thrice and Young Widows
years.p: These Arms Are Snakes tours Easter with [[Thrice|244afcb7-fa9a-49b1-9aa6-0149512d1c52]], [[Planes Mistaken for Stars|ff428f12-1c80-4437-bfff-0e9af6ff94c9]], Mouth of the Architect and [[Young Widows|c9e69e05-2c05-4700-a311-53fe4ffc649e]].

years.h: Headlining Europe, then opening for Mastodon
years.p: These Arms Are Snakes headlines a European tour, then comes home to open for [[Against Me!|a66ebddc-ff04-46b8-820a-15c63e80dba1]] and [[Mastodon|bc5e2ad6-0a4a-4d90-b911-e9a7e6861727]].

years.h: Brian Cook joins [[Russian Circles|cca40a67-e959-46f8-a3f3-8a3f77d2da9e]]
years.p: Brian Cook becomes bassist of the Chicago instrumental band Russian Circles while still in These Arms Are Snakes, a double life that will shape how the band ends.

eras.title: One month, one last album, one bad night
eras.text: These Arms Are Snakes left Jade Tree for Suicide Squeeze, cut its final album in a month, and scattered songs across splits with friends. Then it stopped, faster than anyone planned.

years.h: Splits with [[Pelican|5a797e16-f69a-4957-820f-1152ec19d236]], Russian Circles and Tropics
years.p: These Arms Are Snakes shares records with Pelican (Hydra Head), Russian Circles (Sargent House) and Tropics (We-Be). Ryan Frederiksen also starts [[Narrows|3a9bf775-66f1-4299-b062-5cb0585d5672]] with Botch singer Dave Verellen.

years.h: Tail Swallower and Dove on Suicide Squeeze
years.p: Recorded at Red Room with Chris Common in one month, the fastest album the band made. The band praised Suicide Squeeze's marketing and its roster of friends like [[Minus the Bear|c1e98e4a-4628-4c89-a7a6-0e0171600b05]].
years.xp: The third and final album moves away from the band's hardcore roots toward stranger textures and more traditional song shapes. Pitchfork gave it 6.4.

years.h: A split 7-inch with All the Saints on Touch and Go
years.p: These Arms Are Snakes' last new release while active comes out as a limited split 7-inch with All the Saints on Touch and Go.

years.big: The gear gave out, and so did the band
q: Our final show was sort of unceremonious, our gear kind of crapped out
years.h: These Arms Are Snakes announces its breakup on Christmas
years.p: These Arms Are Snakes had been talking about writing a fourth album that December. Instead it announced on Christmas Day that it was done.
years.xp:
Brian Cook later told Noisey the end was abrupt and messy, with Russian Circles pulling on him at the same time. The last show went badly when the band's equipment failed, and the farewell shows they talked about never happened.

Cook said the lack of a proper ending bothered him for years.

eras.title: The songs left in the drawer
eras.text: Unreleased These Arms Are Snakes recordings kept surfacing years after the breakup, and the band that swore never to reunite ended up playing Seattle twice.

years.h: Their Nirvana cover escapes after seven years
years.p: The band's version of Nirvana's Heart-Shaped Box, shelved since the breakup, finally appears on Robotic Empire's In Utero, in Tribute, in Entirety.

years.h: A Lost Sounds cover on a split with [[The Coathangers|60698f82-b047-48a4-8612-8e9bde5b5fd4]]
years.p: The song meant for a Minus the Bear split that never happened, a cover of Lost Sounds' Energy Drink and the Long Walk Home, comes out on Suicide Squeeze with the Coathangers.
years.xp: Brian Cook told Noisey this was the last finished These Arms Are Snakes recording still in the vault, apart from an old four-song demo. Asked about a reunion, he said he'd always said never, but the others had told him to stop saying that.

years.h: A secret reunion show at Barboza, Seattle
years.p: These Arms Are Snakes plays a secret show at Barboza with Constant Lovers, Merso and Dust Moth. On drums: Ben Verellen, the 2005 drummer who had quit without a word.

years.h: A second reunion show, this time announced
years.p: These Arms Are Snakes plays a publicly announced show in Seattle, twelve years after the breakup.

years.h: Duct Tape & Shivering Crows empties the vault
years.p: Suicide Squeeze collects These Arms Are Snakes' split tracks, compilation songs and the four-song demo recorded before This Is Meant to Hurt You. The same year, Brian Cook's old band [[Botch|72448406-ba82-43a7-9e13-d9a47ff333f4]] reunites.
